justification: Contributes a tunable dialogue policy planner that decides the next dialogue strategy; evaluated only in lab experiments on three proactive-dialogue applications with simulated interaction, not deployed.

Novelty is ProgVe, self-generated self-executing verification pseudo-programs producing the judgement (ProgRe refinement is the runner-up); evidence is lab runs on three instruction-following and math benchmarks.

Contributes a graph formalism for generating, aggregating and refining candidate LLM thoughts, generalising Tree of Thoughts; evidence is lab comparisons against CoT/ToT on constructed tasks such as sorting.

Contribution is turning citation/hallucination assessments into actionable natural-language feedback that drives iterative refinement; validated in the lab on ASQA, ELI5 and QAMPARI, with no deployed use.

FDSP's claim is the injection of targeted external static-analysis feedback so the LLM rewrites vulnerable code, beating self-feedback; validated on the authors' new PythonSecurityEval dataset in the lab.
The loop rewrites the agent's own prompt and in-context examples through feedback-driven critique and synthesis across episodes; evidence is lab performance across 45 tasks plus a cost analysis.

Contribution is distilled critic models whose feedback drives a refiner in a critique-refine loop; validated in the lab on three Indic simplification settings, with human raters as the headline measuring instrument.

Claim is step-level rather than trajectory-level self-critique feeding action refinement (MCTS is the carrier, runner-up); evidence is lab benchmark runs on WebShop and HotPotQA plus self-training iterations.

CodeTree contributes a unified tree over coding strategies with ranking, expansion and termination decisions guiding exploration; validated in the lab on seven code-generation benchmarks including SWEBench.
Studies self-debugging driven by self-generated tests, and locates the effect in test-induced bias in the check itself; an empirical lab investigation over self-contained Python programming tasks.
The headline artefact is ECCO, a reproducible benchmark and harness for measuring code efficiency, used to compare three existing loop approaches in the lab rather than to propose a new mechanism.
PREFER's feedback-reflect-refine loop rewrites the prompts themselves and synthesises new weak learners across boosting rounds; validated in lab experiments across multiple task types.

Mirror's object is the reflection step, diversifying reflection directions so revision does not stall at one iteration (Navigator/Reasoner roles are carriers); lab evaluation on five reasoning datasets.
Novelty is a learned advantage function that judges before execution whether a proposed action helps, replacing physical verification; validated in the lab on Overcooked-AI and a RoCoBench variant.

ProCo's contribution is the verification device, masking a key condition and predicting it to test a response before correcting; validated in the lab on QA, arithmetic and commonsense reasoning datasets.
CoT-SelfEvolve iteratively rewrites code from executor traceback feedback structured as a chain of thought, so the object is the correction; validated in the lab on the DS-1000 dataset.

PIT reformulates the RLHF objective so the model learns an improvement policy from preference data rather than being prompted to refine; validated in lab experiments on two real-world and one synthetic dataset.

Sherlock trains a trajectory-level self-correction objective and then keeps improving on its own outputs without external supervision, an outer loop over the model; lab evaluation across eight benchmarks.

The hierarchical reasoning module learns when to halt and allocates a different number of reasoning cycles per input; a prototype compact model with lab results on reasoning tasks, not used in practice.
Measures intrinsic self-correction of reasoning, the revision step, by injecting synthetic perturbations into chain-of-thought and observing corrections across open-weight models in a lab probe.
Chain of Self-Correction stages a generate-execute-verify-correct cycle fine-tuned into the model, with the correction sequence as the claim; validated in the lab on standard mathematical datasets.

Contributes a pipeline that collects self-critiques and fine-tunes small models to refine their own solutions, with verifier strength as a limiting condition; lab experiments on five math and commonsense datasets.
Argues theoretically and empirically that intrinsic self-correction works, isolating zero temperature and fair prompts as the conditions; lab experiments varying those factors across existing LLMs.
Decomposes intrinsic self-correction into detection, localisation and correction and audits that one mechanism; cross-model lab runs on GSM8K-Complex with an error-hint condition deliberately varied.
APR contributes spawn/join control-flow machinery letting the model orchestrate serialised and parallel inference threads (search shape is the runner-up); lab results on the Countdown reasoning task.
